messages:
Ava (CEO): thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. i'll hang here for 20 mins to answer clarifying q's about mission, positioning, and the roadmap. drop short questions and i'll try to keep answers concise :sparkles:
Diego (Eng): thanks! quick one — when you say 'unified runtime' are we prioritizing single codepath or compatibility across multiple runtimes?
Ava (CEO): great q — priority is stable developer surface + predictable economics. that means a single API/contract for customers, while internally we support multiple optimized execution paths. customers shouldn't need to care about kernel choices.
Liam (Sales): from GTM — how do we talk about competitors who bundle models + infra? sales team needs a 2-line differentiator.
Maya (Head of Strategy): 2-line: "We make serving LLMs predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so teams hit latency, cost, and compliance targets without building infra." emphasize operational primitives (SLA, rollouts, cost controls).
Chris (VP Product): also call out our smart routing + fallback story — it keeps apps online during model or capacity issues. customers actually care about graceful degradation.
Diego (Eng): are we committing to supporting every popular quantized format? eg q4_* variants across toolchains.
Chris (VP Product): we won't chase every permutation at parity. roadmap: support the major community formats that unlock 90% of throughput wins, provide a plugin/compat layer for others. we'll publish compatibility matrix in docs.
Liam (Sales): price/how to position vs big clouds on cost? customers ask "why pay you AND cloud".
Ava (CEO): answer: we sell predictability + operational efficiency. unit cost may be lower in Dedicated because of batching/caching and quantization guidance. plus features clouds don't offer out of box: token-level cost attribution, rollout controls, private deployment integrations. also partner with cloud infra so customers can keep compute where they want.
Maya (Head of Strategy): add: our moat is ops + observability. models commoditize; serving well doesn't.
Diego (Eng): any changes to the roadmap after today re: Private on-prem timeline?
Ava (CEO): timeline unchanged — pilot customers in Q2, GA in Q4. priority: KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
Liam (Sales): customer asks about model ownership — if they want to bring a custom finetuned model, is that supported?
Chris (VP Product): yes — Dedicated/Private support customer models with version pinning + canary rollouts. Hosted supports vetted customer model uploads under an enterprise plan (security review).
Diego (Eng): tiny nit — can we get a short blurb the growth team can use in pitch decks re: single-sentence mission?
Maya (Head of Strategy): "Redwood Inference: the production platform that makes running LLMs predictable, economical, and secure across any infrastructure." short + to the point.
Ava (CEO): perfect. i'll post this blurb in the marketing channel and in the all-hands notes. thanks all — if there are deeper product or competitive dives, book time with maya/chris.
OpsBot: deploy-bot posted: deployment redwood-console-v2 rolled to staging at 1765843300 :rocket: (no failures)
Diego (Eng): thanks — logging this convo into the roadmap thread for traceability.
Liam (Sales): thanks ava, maya — super helpful. :thumbsup:
